solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Buzzer initially put in behind drawer in pub

parts.note: a bee buzzes, so it is a buzzer

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word for behind

parts.note: the rump is the behind, the backside

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word put

parts.note: first letter P

explanation.surface: An insect starts something behind a drawer in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is not furniture but something that draws, here beer from the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer pump is the handle a barman pulls to draw ale, so it is a drawer of beer in a pub.

clue.text: Resist responsibility often passed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a trend is to resist it
second meaning: passing the ... is shifting responsibility

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom pass the buck means to shift blame or duty to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for opposing something and the noun in the idiom for evading duty.

clue.text: Ages of sailing ships halved

indicators.note: halved means the word for sailing ships loses its front half, keeping only the back

parts.note: galleons are large old sailing ships

explanation.surface: Old sailing ships cut in two after ages at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long periods of time, so ages.

clue.text: Representation of power in speech gripping board

indicators.note: gripping means the spoken word holds the board inside it

parts.note: oral means spoken, in speech
a tray is a flat board for carrying things

explanation.surface: A speech about power that grips the board of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' looks like a company board, but it is a flat tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction or rendering of someone, a representation of them.

clue.text: In small way, limit care provision

parts.note: mini means small
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to ration is to limit supply

explanation.surface: Rationing care services in a small way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministration is the giving of help or care, especially to the sick or needy.

clue.text: Host swallowing wine gum

indicators.note: swallowing means the host takes the wine inside itself

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A party host gulps down wine and then some gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from the mastic tree, used as a chewing gum and a varnish.

clue.text: Oil processed into fine condiment

indicators.note: into means the rearranged oil goes inside the word for fine

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate, fine

indicators.note: processed means the letters of oil are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Oil is processed into a fine sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, written AI, is a common crossword shorthand for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise, a sauce served alongside food.

clue.text: Nothing to be gained by mixing untrained workers together

indicators.note: mixing means the letters of untrained plus O are stirred into a new order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: No benefit from mixing untrained staff in with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be gained by' says the O is added to the letters of untrained before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is an organised association of employees acting collectively.

clue.text: Recycling of map that monks produce

indicators.note: of here means the recycling word comes after the map word, belonging to it

parts.note: a chart is a map
recycling is reuse

explanation.surface: Recycling the maps that monks drew.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a liqueur made by Carthusian monks at their monastery near Grenoble.

clue.text: Contend with cold at seaside

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
on the front means on the seafront, at the seaside

explanation.surface: Coping with the chill of a seaside promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront a problem is to face up to it, to tackle it head on.

clue.text: Everything jolly presumably in yearly foreign hotel

indicators.note: in places the phrase inside the abbreviation for yearly

parts.note: PA is per annum, yearly
if there is O (nothing) SAD, everything is presumably jolly

explanation.surface: A cheerful annual stay at a hotel abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful middle phrase is read as O SAD: with zero sadness, all must be jolly.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is an inn in Spanish-speaking countries, so a hotel abroad for an English solver.

clue.text: Old order from EEC remaining uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain means the letters are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: The old European order of the EEC remains uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: The EEC was the European Economic Community, forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancien régime was the political system of France before the 1789 Revolution, the old order.

clue.text: Quiet grudge I held in fearful anticipation

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: held in means the I is kept inside the word for grudge

parts.note: resentment is a grudge held against someone

explanation.surface: Someone quietly nursing a grudge with a sense of dread.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a foreboding, an intuitive feeling that something bad is about to happen.

clue.text: In a journey, part of the eye that helps night vision

indicators.note: In at the start means the eye part is placed inside the journey

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air
a lash is an eyelash

explanation.surface: On a journey, part of the eye helps one see at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashlight is a torch, a hand-held lamp for seeing in the dark.

clue.text: No charisma needed to play these?

definitions.text: No charisma needed to play these?

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters of no charisma are played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: You need no personal magnetism to play mouth organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonicas are mouth organs, instruments anyone can play without star quality.

clue.text: Straight line's drawn in a fine green

indicators.note: drawn in means the other letters are pulled inside the line

parts.note: a ley line is a supposed straight line linking ancient sites; the 's is has
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An artist draws a straight line in a fine shade of green.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafy describes a place full of trees and foliage, hence green and verdant.

clue.text: Drops perhaps after this ritual exercise

definitions.text: Drops perhaps after this ritual exercise

parts.words: Drops perhaps after this ritual exercise
parts.note: a ceremonial dance performed in the hope that raindrops will follow

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drops' suggests collapsing from exhaustion after exercise, but the drops are raindrops the ritual summons.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial dance performed to bring on wet weather, so drops follow it.

clue.text: Activity during sleep contributes to fair amount lost

indicators.note: contributes to means the sleep activity is put inside the word for fair

parts.note: decent means fair, reasonable
REM, rapid eye movement, happens during dreaming sleep

explanation.surface: Sleep contributes a fair amount to weight lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrement is a decrease, the quantity by which something is reduced.

clue.text: Son, naughty boy, left school a dunce

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
an imp is a mischievous child
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A mischievous son leaves school a dunce.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish, slow-witted person, much like a dunce.

clue.text: Get on the wrong side of mule, say

definitions.text: Get on the wrong side of
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to annoy or oppose someone
second meaning: a hybrid, as a mule is a horse-donkey hybrid

explanation.walkthrough: A mule is famously stubborn, so getting on its wrong side sounds natural; it is just an example of a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for thwarting someone and a noun for an animal bred from two species.

clue.text: Tall cavalry displacing small dockers

parts.note: long means tall

indicators.note: displacing means the small letter shifts to a new spot within the word for cavalry

parts.note: cavalry are soldiers on horseback, horsemen

explanation.surface: Tall cavalrymen push aside small dockers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displacing' moves the S of HORSEMEN to the front, giving SHOREMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Longshoremen load and unload ships at a port, the American word for dock workers.

clue.text: South American native that's on slippery slope

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A South American native on a slippery slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase, but South gives S and American native is the Cree.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is loose broken rock on a mountainside, slippery underfoot.

clue.text: Doctor comes to a halt

indicators.note: comes to means the doctor is followed by the next letter

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC time-travelling hero

explanation.surface: A doctor comes to a stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running British TV science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call to stop a horse, an order to halt.

clue.text: For example, accepting women's influence

indicators.note: accepting means the word for example takes the letter inside

parts.note: say means for example
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Accepting women's influence, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway is power or control over others, as in holding sway.

clue.text: Commanding officer painting racing vehicle

parts.note: GOC is General Officer Commanding
painting is art

explanation.surface: An army commander paints a racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commanding officer' tempts with CO, but the letters needed are GOC, General Officer Commanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-cart is a small low motor vehicle used for kart racing.

clue.text: Minor affair as pig squashes one dilapidated shed

indicators.note: squashes means the pig crams the other letters inside itself

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: dilapidated means the letters of shed are in ruins, rearranged

explanation.surface: A pig flattens a ramshackle shed, a small event on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashes' reads as crushing, but here it means the pig holds the other letters inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a subsidiary attraction or incidental matter, less important than the main event.

clue.text: Sample of police kit Met finally accepted

indicators.note: accepted means the stun gun takes in the letter

parts.note: a Taser is a stun gun carried by police

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of Met

parts.note: last letter T

explanation.surface: The Metropolitan Police finally adopt a sample stun gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small portion offered to try, a sample of something.

clue.text: Moral primer replaced by satire

indicators.note: replaced means the letters of by satire are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: A moral textbook superseded by satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' reads as a single phrase, but 'by' belongs with satire as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval bestiary described animals to teach Christian moral lessons, a kind of moral instruction book.
